The package requires **mgcv** 1.9-3 or later. The table reflects regression tests
and targeted fitting checks on mgcv 1.9-3 through 1.9-5. **Tested** denotes a
route exercised by the package regression suite. **Checked** denotes a route
exercised on a smooth-model fixture. A dash denotes an unavailable route.
The checks use free smoothing parameters and verify the criterion that actually ran.

| Family | Class | `gam()` REML / ML | `gam()` NCV / QNCV | Ordinary `bam()` REML / ML / fREML | Discrete `bam()` fREML / NCV |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `betabinomial()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `cgamma()` | Extended | Tested / Tested | Checked / Checked | Checked / Checked / Tested | Tested / Checked |
| `cgammals()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `clognormal()` | Extended | Tested / Tested | Tested / Checked | Checked / Checked / Tested | Tested / Tested |
| `clognormalls()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `cmp()` | Extended | Tested / Checked | Checked / Checked | Checked / Checked / Tested | Tested / Checked |
| `cmpls()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `cumulative_link()` | Extended | Tested / Tested | Tested / Checked | Tested / Tested / Tested | Tested / Tested |
| `dirichlet()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `dirmult()` | General | Tested (EFS) / — | — / — | — / — / — | — / — |
| `gpd()` | General | Tested / — | Tested¹ / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `gpoisson()` | Extended | Tested / Tested | Tested² / Tested² | Checked / Checked / Tested | Tested / Checked |
| `log_logistic()` | Extended | Tested / Tested | Tested / Checked | Tested / Tested / Tested | Tested / Tested |
| `log_logisticls()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `nbls()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `ordbeta()` | Extended | Tested / Tested | Tested / Tested | Tested / Tested / Tested | Tested / Tested |
| `pig()` | Extended | Tested / Tested | Tested / Checked | Tested / Tested / Tested | Tested / Tested |
| `pigls()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `zanb()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |
| `zinb()` | General | Tested / — | Tested / Tested | — / — / — | — / — |

¹ An NCV deletion for `gpd()` can move a held-out excess outside the fitted
support. Such a trial has infinite score. QNCV uses a local quadratic
approximation around the full-data predictors.

² Estimated dispersion can make the outer NCV or QNCV optimization sensitive
to the dataset for `gpoisson()`. Check `fit$outer.info$conv` as well as
`fit$converged` and any warnings.

## Engine and criterion details

- **General families.** Use `gam()` for models with several predictors.
  mgcv changes an ML request for a general family to REML. It routes GCV,
  GACV, Pearson likelihood criteria, and fREML requests for these extended
  and general families to REML in `gam()`. Check `fit$method`.
- **Ordinary BAM.** With `discrete = FALSE`, the extended families in the
  table also exercised `GCV.Cp`, `GACV.Cp`, `P-REML`, and `P-ML` on
  smooth-model fixtures. With fixed unit scale both `GCV.Cp` and
  `GACV.Cp` use UBRE, and the working-model Pearson likelihood methods
  reduce to REML and ML. Use `scale = 1` with these families. A default-scale
  request can cause mgcv to label UBRE as GCV and to count an extra
  scale parameter in `logLik()`.
- **Discrete BAM.** mgcv supports fREML and NCV here, including NCV on
  1.9-3. An NCV request to ordinary `bam()` enables discretization.
  A discrete request with another criterion disables discretization.
  Check `fit$dinfo` as well as `fit$method`. Discrete NCV uses the
  working linear model, so its estimates can differ from `gam()` NCV.
  With `cumulative_link()` and a formula offset, supply only the
  predictors and offset variables to `predict()` or use
  `predict(..., discrete = FALSE)` if mgcv's discrete prediction rejects
  `newdata` containing the response.
- **Optimizers.** `dirmult()` uses extended Fellner--Schall (EFS), which
  mgcv selects automatically for this family. Its first and second
  derivatives support EFS. NCV and outer REML optimization would require
  higher derivatives. NCV and QNCV for general families use outer BFGS.
  Entirely unpenalized ML fits with `gpoisson()` or cauchit
  `cumulative_link()` can hit a native solver limitation in mgcv.
- **Neighbourhoods.** `betabinomial()` deletes whole rows, with each row
  representing a binomial group. Its trial totals follow the response rows
  in deletion and prediction subsets. The tests for general families include
  offsets in both predictors, repeated prediction indices, and a nonunit
  `gamma`. Use `nei` to specify neighbourhoods for dependent observations.
- **Numerical limits.** `cmp()` and `cmpls()` are pure-R reference
  implementations with adaptive summation and numerical limits on the
  supported parameter range. The BAM checks for `cmp()` establish
  correctness on small fixtures. Censoring and extreme-value families also
  have parameter-dependent numerical or support limits. See each family
  help page for its response encoding, links, and prediction scale.

The family-specific tests live in `tests/`. The joint
`tests/gamlss-ncv.R` checks held-out derivatives for several general
families. The individual family tests cover fitted state, likelihood
reporting, derivatives, and distribution callbacks.
